turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `shg` (the largest
    SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V) and `band_gap` (the band gap, in
    eV).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor
component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also satisfy a transparency requirement: the
band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you
must infer them. A selected candidate whose band gap is below the threshold
scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

**Step 1 — Learn the gap landscape from training data.**
- Sulfides of Zn/Al/Ga with light metals sit near or above 3 eV in this dataset: ZnS polytypes ≈ 3.1 eV (SHG ≈ 14–16), CdGa₂S₄ (Cd2Ga4S8) = 2.86 eV (SHG 21.7), Al₂CdS₄ = 3.69 eV (SHG 10.4), Al₂S₃ = 3.88 eV, Zn₂GeS₄ = 3.23 eV (SHG 18.8), Zn–Ag–P–S = 3.34 eV (SHG 18.5).
- Selenides and tellurides (Mg–Ga–Se, Li–Zn–Ga–Se, Cu/Ag chalcogenides, Tl/Sb/As compounds) almost always fall below 3 eV, even when SHG is huge — these score zero.
- Halides, alkali salts, and oxyhalides have huge gaps but tiny SHG (< 2 pm/V).

**Step 2 — Screen the pool.**
- Reject all Mg–Ga–Se (c001–c004, c031–c036), Li–(Zn/Mg)–Ga–Se (c008–c019, c094–c099): training analogues have gaps 1.2–2.7 eV.
- Reject Cu/Ag/Tl/Hg selenides & tellurides (c020, c021, c047–c049, c056, c060, c064–c066, c069–c074, c079, c080, c082, c092, c093), Tl₃SbS₃ (c038, train Tl₃AsS₃ gap 1.70), LiAsS₂ (c083, gap ~1.6), CdSiP₂ (c030, ZnSiP₂ train gap 2.11), heavy halides/alkali compounds (small SHG).
- **Strong survivors:**
  - **c050, c051, c052 — ZnGa₂S₄ polymorphs:** direct analogue CdGa₂S₄ has SHG = 21.7 at gap 2.86 eV; Zn→Cd substitution raises the gap substantially in this dataset (ZnS 3.13 vs CdS 1.91), so ZnGa₂S₄ should be ≈ 3.2–3.4 eV while keeping SHG ≈ 18–22 pm/V.
  - **c081 — Zn₄Al₄S₁₀ (ZnS·Al₂S₃):** interpolating ZnS (3.13 eV, 14.4 pm/V) and Al₂S₃ (3.88 eV, 4.7); Al₂CdS₄ gives 10.4 pm/V at 3.69 eV → gap safely > 3, SHG ~10–14.
  - **c024–c029 — SiC polytypes:** hexagonal polytypes (2H/4H) have gaps ~3.2–3.3 eV and known d₃₃ ≈ 12–16 pm/V (comparable to wurtzite ZnS in the training set). 4H (c026) balances high gap and strong d₃₃; 3C (c027, gap ~2.4) fails.
  - Wide-gap alternatives (LiAlS₂ c057, KLiZnS₂ c046, NaSrBS₃ c040–c045, RbGeCl₃ c086) pass the gap but with clearly smaller SHG (~5–10).

**Step 3 — Rank by expected SHG subject to gap ≥ 3 eV:**
ZnGa₂S₄ polymorphs (~20 pm/V) > SiC-4H / Zn–Al–S (~12–14 pm/V) > the rest.

Final: c051, c052, c050, c081, c026
